# csv2sql

Command-line CSV to SQL converter. Reads a `.csv`, infers column types, and
writes a `CREATE TABLE` plus batched `INSERT` statements.

Java 8, no dependencies, no build tool. `./build.sh` and you're done.

```sh
./build.sh
./csv2sql -i data/users.csv -t users -o users.sql
sqlite3 app.db < users.sql
```

Or from a pipe:

```sh
cat data.csv | ./csv2sql -t users > users.sql
```

`./csv2sql --help` lists every option. `./test.sh` builds and runs the suite.

## Example

`examples/users.csv` in, this out:

```sql
-- generated by csv2sql from examples/users.csv
-- id INTEGER, first_name TEXT, ...; inferred from 6 row(s)
CREATE TABLE "users" (
  "id" INTEGER,
  "first_name" TEXT,
  "age" BIGINT,
  "active" BOOLEAN,
  "signup_date" DATE,
  "last_login" TIMESTAMP,
  "balance" DECIMAL(16,5),
  "notes" TEXT);
INSERT INTO "users" ("id", "first_name", ...)
VALUES (1,'Ada','Lovelace','ada@example.com',36,TRUE,'1843-12-10',...),
  (2,'Grace','Hopper','grace@example.com',85,FALSE,'1952-01-01',...),
  ...
```

## How it works

**Parsing** is RFC 4180: quoted fields, `""` for a literal quote, delimiters and
newlines inside quotes, and `\n` / `\r\n` / `\r` line endings. A UTF-8 BOM is
stripped. Ragged rows are padded with `NULL` or truncated, and the count is
reported on stderr rather than aborting the run.

**Type inference** reads the first `--sample-size` rows (default 1000) and only
widens: `INTEGER` → `BIGINT` → `DECIMAL` → `TEXT`. Dates and timestamps must be
ISO-8601. `true`/`false`/`yes`/`no` become `BOOLEAN`, written back as
`TRUE`/`FALSE`. `DECIMAL(p,s)` is sized to the widest value seen, so nothing
rounds.

**Memory** is bounded by the sample, not the file. The sampled rows are held
back to describe the data in the DDL; the rest streams straight through.
200k rows convert in under a second inside a 48 MB heap.

One consequence worth knowing: because inference only sees a sample, a later row
can hold a value that doesn't fit its column. The tool quotes those rather than
emitting them bare, so you get a type error naming the bad value instead of a
syntax error that takes down the whole multi-row `INSERT`.

**Quoting** is dialect-aware. Identifiers are always quoted, so reserved words
(`select`) and odd headers (`User Name`) need no special handling; duplicates
become `id`, `id_2`. MySQL gets backtick identifiers and backslash escaping,
everything else doubles single quotes.

## Options

| Option | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `-i, --input <path>` | CSV to read, or `-` for stdin (default `-`) |
| `-o, --output <path>` | File to write, or `-` for stdout (default `-`) |
| `-t, --table <name>` | Target table name |
| `--dialect <name>` | `standard` (default), `mysql`, `postgres`, `sqlite`, `none` |
| `--delimiter <x>` | `auto` (default), `csv`, `tsv`, `semicolon`, `pipe`, or one char |
| `--quote` / `--escape <c>` | Override the quote and escape characters |
| `--no-header` | Every row is data; columns become `col1`, `col2`, ... |
| `--empty-as-string` | Write empty cells as `''` instead of `NULL` |
| `--drop-table` | Emit `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS` first |
| `--truncate` | Emit `TRUNCATE TABLE` after the DDL |
| `--no-create-table` | Emit only `INSERT`s (alias: `--data-only`) |
| `--schema-only` | Emit only the `CREATE TABLE` |
| `--transaction` | Wrap in `BEGIN` / `COMMIT` |
| `--batch-size <n>` | Rows per multi-row `INSERT` (default 100) |
| `--sample-size <n>` | Rows to inspect for types; `0` makes every column `TEXT` |
| `--lower-case-names` | Lowercase generated column names |
| `--compact` | One statement per line |
| `--no-comments` | Drop the generated-by header |
| `--encoding <cs>` | Input and output charset (default UTF-8) |

Flags compose rather than override each other: `--data-only --drop-table` emits
the `DROP` and the `INSERT`s, skipping only the `CREATE TABLE`.

## Common uses

Re-importing a file so the load is repeatable:

```sh
./csv2sql -i users.csv -t users --drop-table --transaction -o users.sql
```

Schema and data separately, for a staging table:

```sh
./csv2sql -i users.csv -t users --schema-only > schema.sql
./csv2sql -i users.csv -t users --data-only   > data.sql
```

Targeting MySQL:

```sh
./csv2sql -i users.csv -t users --dialect mysql -o users.sql
```

## Layout

| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `CsvToSql.java` | Entry point, statement assembly, streaming |
| `CsvReader.java` | RFC 4180 reader |
| `Delimiters.java` | Delimiter sniffing |
| `SqlType.java` | Type classification and widening |
| `Column.java` | Per-column type tracking, literal rendering |
| `SqlDialect.java` | Identifier and string quoting per database |
| `Options.java` | Command-line parsing |
